audit_findings.title: The bridge omits $54.2 million of liquid Treasury notes
audit_findings.magnitude: $54.244 million, equal to $2.12 per diluted share and 10.7% of the $506 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The Treasury notes belong in the non-operating asset bridge because investment interest is purged from OE; omitting them understates the common-equity claim.
audit_findings.evidence: Our long-term investments consist of U.S. Treasury notes, with maturities ranging between one and two years, and total $ 54.2 million at June 30, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated omission: the $133.25 million bridge balance equals filed cash of $73.628 million plus short-term investments of $59.622 million and therefore excludes the separately filed $54.244 million of long-term Treasury notes. Adding the full amount would raise base value from $19.72 to approximately $21.84 per share and bull value from $22.33 to approximately $24.45, which can change the valuation conclusion. The amount ultimately addable remains subject to the excess-cash review.
audit_findings.action: Confirm no part of the $54.244 million was included elsewhere, identify any restricted or operationally committed portion, and rerun all scenarios with the uncommitted balance added to the bridge.

audit_findings.title: FY2026 earnings may not reflect the forward tariff run rate
audit_findings.magnitude: $15.0 million filed annual gross tariff exposure and $5.0 million FY2026 tariff recovery; net-of-pricing OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The $5.0 million recovery may inflate anchor OE, while the difference between FY2026 tariff expense and the forward net tariff burden may reduce normalized OE and future growth cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: Based on current operating levels, we estimate our annual tariff exposure to be approximately $15.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates both a $5.0 million benefit in FY2026 gross profit and a $15.0 million estimated annual tariff exposure. Those amounts equal approximately 19% and 57% of the $26.5 million OE anchor, respectively, so the issue is reasonably capable of changing value. It remains unresolved whether the refund was already removed from OE, how much tariff cost FY2026 already contained, and how much pricing and sourcing mitigation offsets the forward burden.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the OE anchor to remove the after-tax effect of the $5.0 million recovery, calculate FY2026 tariffs already expensed, estimate the post-year-end annual tariff burden net of documented pricing and sourcing offsets, and rerun every scenario using normalized OE.

audit_findings.title: The entire cash and short-term investment balance may not be excess cash
audit_findings.mechanism: Any minimum operating-cash reserve must be removed from the $133.25 million non-operating asset addition to the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We believe our cash, cash equivalents and investments are available to meet short-term liquidity needs.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation adds all $133.25 million even though the filing describes cash and investments as available to meet liquidity needs and reports $148.463 million of inventory, $62.730 million of customer deposits, $42.0 million of purchase commitments, and fiscal 2027 capital spending of $12–14 million. These facts establish operating demands but do not establish the required reserve or prove that a material portion is unavailable to owners. The possible effect is therefore material in capacity but unquantified on the present record.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a minimum-cash analysis covering seasonal working capital, customer-deposit obligations, purchase commitments, capital expenditures, foreign cash constraints, and liquidity variability; rerun the bridge using only demonstrably surplus cash and investments.

audit_findings.title: A nonrecurring contract-termination receipt may remain in anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, the after-tax termination fee raises the $26.5 million latest-year OE anchor and is capitalized through forecast OE and terminal value despite being nonrecurring.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest and other income, net increased 15.3% due to a contract termination fee received during the first quarter of fiscal 2026 from our former private label credit card provider.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates receipt of the nonrecurring fee but does not disclose its amount or the supplied OE reconciliation. Although FY2026 interest and other income was $8.388 million and investment interest was $6.4 million, their difference also contains foreign-exchange and other items, so it cannot establish the fee amount. Materiality cannot be determined until the fee and its treatment in OE are identified.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the general-ledger or filing reconciliation for the termination fee, verify whether it was excluded separately from investment interest, calculate its tax effect, and rerun the valuation if any net amount remains in anchor OE.

audit_findings.title: Working-capital consumption may be absent from the owner-earnings numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2026 operating-asset and liability changes consumed $37.7 million, including an $8.435 million inventory increase and a $12.338 million reduction in customer deposits; normalized requirement unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Normalized working-capital reinvestment should reduce OE directly or be captured consistently by the growth-and-RONTA reinvestment charge; omission raises OE, while counting it in both places would understate value.
audit_findings.evidence: Working capital changes during fiscal 2026 were from increased inventory carrying levels along with a reduction in customer deposits.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash requirement is demonstrated and is larger than the $26.5 million OE anchor, but the filing attributes part of it to new products, price increases, and declining orders, so the full $37.7 million is not necessarily recurring. The record also does not show whether anchor OE or the 9% RONTA mechanism already captures normalized working capital. The direction is overstatement if omitted, but the material recurring amount remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Produce the FY2026 OE reconciliation and the invested-capital base used for the 9% RONTA calculation; separate structural working-capital needs from temporary movements, verify no double counting, and rerun with the normalized requirement.

audit_findings.title: Accrued uncertain-tax claims are not visible in the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.842 million of gross unrecognized tax benefits plus $0.7 million of accrued interest and penalties, totaling $4.542 million or approximately $0.18 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: A probable cash settlement not already borne by forecast OE would reduce bridge cash or require a separate liability deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: As of June 30, 2026, we had gross unrecognized tax benefits of $ 3.8 million related to uncertain tax positions in various jurisdictions.
audit_findings.explanation: Even deducting the entire disclosed $4.542 million would reduce the $506 million base equity value by only 0.9%, from $19.72 to approximately $19.54 per share, and the $13.80 buy-below level by approximately $0.12 per share. That is small relative to the $67–91 million differences between adjacent scenario values. The actual adverse amount is likely lower because $1.2 million may resolve within twelve months and recognition of $1.0 million of that amount would reduce the effective tax rate.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the balance-sheet accounts containing the tax liability and accrued interest, identify any probable settlement omitted from projected OE, and document the bridge treatment; no full valuation rerun is needed unless new evidence materially increases the exposure.
